<description>
This implements the Consensus Cleanup validation rules proposed in [BIP 54](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0054.md). These rules are only enabled on regtest. Mainnet activation, if any, is to be considered separately.

This patchset is based on the code that was previously reviewed ([1](https://github.com/bitcoin-inquisition/bitcoin/pull/99), [2](https://github.com/bitcoin-inquisition/bitcoin/pull/110)) and tested (for instance [here](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/consensus-cleanup-demo-of-slow-blocks-on-signet/2367)) on Bitcoin Inquisition. The tests and documentation have since been improved, but the consensus-critical commits have been carried over with only minor differences (the only behavioural one being the addition of the stripped-size check to `PreChecks`).

Roughly 95% of the added lines are tests or test data. The format, contents, and reproduction procedure for the BIP 54 test vectors are documented [here](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/tree/master/bip-0054/test_vectors). The `bip54_tests` unit test module exercises each mitigation extensively in isolation. The `feature_bip54.py` functional test verifies all of them end-to-end after and prior to activation. For the timestamp rules, it simulates timewarp and Murch–Zawy attacks, demonstrating the new timestamp rules prevent these exploits. A fuzz harness for the sigop accounting logic is also included, which can be seeded from the BIP test vectors (implemented [here](https://github.com/darosior/bitcoin/tree/bip54_seed_fuzz_corpus)).

See commit messages for details.
</description>

[2026-11-23] rc:4672543560 inline on src/validation.cpp by ariard (contributor) (edited 2026-11-23):
This new consensus sanitization check is stateless, that it whatever the inclusion height of the coinbase, after the activation of BIP54, the nSequence of the 1st input should NOT be equal to `SEQUENCE_FINAL`.

There is nothing which is context-dependent or even tx-structure dependent (like the BIP141 commitment which is allowed to be in _any_  `scriptpubkey `of the coinbase tx), so this check could be replicated in other code paths to proceed to the early rejection of ill-crafted transactions.

E.g I wonder if the check should be added in `CheckTransaction()` and be used in the `PreChecks()` code path (where `CheckTransaction()` is called before `IsCoinBase()` detection) or in `CheckBlock()` (where we do a `CheckTransaction()`).

I have not test it but lacking to do so, it sounds you can mutate a valid coinbase to alter its nSequence field and provoke the invalidity of the whole block. It sounds there are code paths where `CheckBlock()` is done before `ContextualCheckBlock()` (e.g in `AcceptBlock()`). It sounds as such you might have `CheckBlock()` result where the validity is not wholly complete, at least the state of information that is available in the code path.

There is also the question of compact block (BIP152), the spec says "When in doubt, nodes SHOULD only include the coinbase transaction in prefilledtxn." This is unsure if the compact block validation code already sanitize on the reception of a coinbase (to avoid fulfilling resources after the `CMPCTBLOCK`), I have no re-checked fully, though looking shortly in `blockencoding.cpp` it doesn't sound to.
